name: Monomem
description: Self-hosted shared memory for AI coding agents: one SQLite file on the user's machine, shared by every connected tool. Each note carries a server-stamped writer, version history and undo. Reads and ordinary saves keep Guard's usual handling; archiving, replacing, confirming, merging, history changes, rollback, trust, held writes and the task board are gated on review. Covers the 1.6 tool names and the 1.5 names. Off until you turn it on.
saferAlternatives: No model is called and data stays in the local SQLite file. Semantic search is off by default; if MONOMEM_EMBEDDINGS is turned on and MONOMEM_EMBED_URL points at a remote host, note and search text are sent there.

Monomem 1.6 registers seven tools by default (memory_save, _search, _read, _list, _archive, _replace, _catch_up); the rest need MONOMEM_TOOLS. The 1.5 names still answer for one release and keep their defaults, except memory_history (now review).

This stdio launch runs as the local operator with no key. Writes are stamped written_by "stdio", or "stdio:<app>" when the config sets MONOMEM_CLIENT: a name from the config file, not proof. Per-app keys apply only to the HTTP server, not here.
Over stdio, memory_held, memory_trust and memory_rollback are not offered and approving a task is refused, unless MONOMEM_STDIO_ADMIN_TOOLS=1.

Under the default MONOMEM_LINT policy, known secret formats are refused and injection-like text is held for review; bare high-entropy strings are stored with a warning. MONOMEM_LINT=warn stores all of these, so this holds only by default.

memory_archive hides a note from every agent read; it can be restored. Its text can remain in the database file, the WAL and backups (up to 5 weeks); permanent removal is the operator CLI (monomem delete) or the dashboard. It stays on review.

Guard decides per tool name, so a 1.6 tool with actions takes its strictest one: memory_replace, memory_history, memory_tidy, memory_review and memory_tasks are on review even for read-only actions. The task runner is not in the npm package.

This entry matches the monomem-mcp command (npm i -g monomem; the 1.6 names need 1.6.0 or later), which starts only the stdio MCP server. Launches such as npx -y monomem mcp, node <path>/cli.js mcp or the standalone download keep Guard normal handling.
